The positions match what happened in the parts that set up the game a bot faces: his hands, the board, the opponent's board, points, knockouts and the deck lists. I found no blocker. The two major findings are plan-record problems: a dropped Mesagoza use (R3-F1) and a missing Giga Turbo Energy target (R3-F2). Neither touches the current km3 numbers, because those lines stop at a draw card before the affected step. Every finding can be fixed from the ledger text alone; none needs a frame or the video. From my two games, nothing stands in the way of deleting their frames.

Method: Python scripts in my R3 folder dumped the positions (dump_pos.py → pos_dump.txt) and compact ledger rows (compact.py → c_210041.txt, c_230258.txt). xcheck.py compared each position, in order, with that turn's ledger board_at_start: hand names, both boards (name, current HP, Energy by type, Tool, Special Conditions), points, opponent hand count and Stadium. All 14 matched. It also computed the implied deck count, which I checked against the draw and search trail. I checked the evolution stacks, discards, discard_energy, knockouts, turn_effects and plan steps (indices traced against the changing board) by hand against plays_in_order, automatic events, REVIEW.md and UNCERTAINTIES.json. I looked up every card's printing and function with lib/card.py (cards.sh → cards.txt). I read the converter, normaliser, position_list.py, kw_report.py and forced_runs.py to find causes and effects.

Results by check:
- Deck files: 20 cards, Darkness, the same 15 printings as DECK_USED, the 210041 QR (every printing in the QR's aliases) and the 230258 live snapshot.
- Rules-switch-2: 'no' for all 14 is right by printing. No card in either game is on the switch list; Shattering Crystal and Mesagoza are not on it.
- turn_effects: empty in all 14, which is right. No opponent attack here leaves an effect, X Speed lasts only the opponent's turn, and Arena of Antiquity is carried as the Stadium.
- report_convert.json leaves out none of my 14 turns, which is correct.

Cross-game pointers for the other readers, not checked by me: 'stadium_activation' plays in 210823; 'Attack:Giga Turbo' without a target in 010706 t09, 203719 t07, 210823 t08 and 010003 t09; '(not ended / cut)' on non-empty plans in 010003 t11 and 015659 t13.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Confirmed for KW-261012_210041000-t08. Codex logged his Mesagoza coin as a separate play of kind 'stadium_activation' (order 6, result 'Activate search coin; tails at 269, no card found.'), right after order 5, kind 'stadium', 'Play Mesagoza.'. The converter's nk() does not know the kind 'stadium_activation'; it returns 'other', and no branch of the plan loop handles that, so the step is dropped with no note. The plan should read ... Play:Mesagoza > UseStadium > Attach:1Darkness@0 zone > Attack:Hang Down. The cause is the converter, and the fix comes from the ledger text alone (no frames needed). The other spellings of this play ('stadium_ability', 'stadium_effect', and 'ability' with a Stadium card) all become UseStadium, tails included: 230258 t05, 010003 t01 and t03, 020824 t07, 010706 t09. The engine offers Mesagoza whenever the deck is not empty (stadiums.rs can_use_mesagoza), so the step was legal. In this position nothing in the current runs changes: the forced line is ['Play:Copycat'] alone. Correction to the cross-game pointer: the 210823 ledger does contain 4 'stadium_activation' plays, but only 2 are in his turns (t02 order 5, t04 order 2); the other 2 are the opponent's and never enter a plan. Both of his are dropped. t02 makes no difference (its plan is cut at Professor's Research, step 1). t04 does make a difference: its forced line [Place:Regigigas@2, Attach:1Darkness@0 zone, Retreat:2, Evolve:Alolan Muk@2, Place:Pawniard@3, Play:Copycat] leaves out the UseStadium he played as step 2. So steps 2 to 6 are compared on a state where the Stadium is still unused (km3 picks UseStadium in 1 seed at the Copycat step, and in 2 seeds as its next choice). So this converter defect does touch the current km3 comparison in one position, 210823 t04, which is another reader's game.

findings.cause: Normaliser and converter, in how the deck list is built. DECK_USED.json for 022530 already has a 20-entry list, but it gives only names and 'semantic entity N' variants: no printings and no integer entity_id. So normalize_ledger.py does not build this game's list from QR_DECODE + DECK_LOG_SNAPSHOT (it does that only for 010706, 203719 and 030351). The converter then reads only DECK_USED. It finds no printing for entity 20770, falls back to the database by name, and takes the first of four 60-HP functions. Both packet files that name the printing are ignored.

Method: I dumped all 12 positions (positions_all.json) and both raw TURN_LEDGER.json files as condensed per-turn dumps: hands, draws, plays with result text, automatic events, and board_at_start / board_after for every Pokémon. Scripts are in scratchpad/panel14/R4/ (dump_pos.py, ledger_dump.py, cards*.sh, grepdb.py, forced*.py, crop.ps1). I compared every field by hand against the ledger rows, DECK_USED, QR_DECODE, DECK_LOG_SNAPSHOT, UNCERTAINTIES, PAUSE_GAME and REVIEW.md, looked up cards with lib/card.py and the database, and read the converter code (nk, resolve, opp_pick, the plan builder, deckspec.read_deck) plus normalize_ledger.py to name causes. I used runs_forced (already produced, nothing re-run) to see how each plan replays in the harness. No engine was built or run; nothing was written outside my folder.

Verdict: neither game should lose its frames until R4-F1 (blocker: Dratini B4 116 in the whole 022530 deck and board) and the major findings are fixed or accepted.

- F1 is easy to settle from the packet files alone: QR_DECODE, DECK_LOG_SNAPSHOT and the 030351 deck file all say B4 116.
- F4 (the opponent's second Meowth) and F6 (Elegant Cape) are mistakes in Codex's ledger. I settled both from frames. After deletion only the videos could settle them again, so record the corrections now.
- F2, F3, F5 and F7 are converter limits that the ledger text alone settles.

Checked and found right in both games:
- points, knock-out counts (1 after Glimmora t09 and after Druddigon t08; no checkup knock-outs in these games) and conditions (Poison on the right Mega Pidgeot ex at t10, cleared by retreat at t12)
- Stadium and owner, Energy now and next, hand counts, discard piles and the implied deck count (210823 t12 deck_count 0 matches the failed draw)

Also noted:
